sentences.text: 2. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 376(1) of IPC and under Section 4 of POCSO Act, in connection with Special POCSO Case No.19 of 2022.

He has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twelve years with a fine of Rs.10,000/-, for the offence under Sections 376(1) of IPC.
3.

Heard, learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4.
Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.

5. The allegation against the appellant is that on the pretext of marriage, the appellant had entered into physical relationship with the victim and further, he and the other family members on the aforesaid assurance used to take house work from the victim.
6.
From the evidence, we find that year of birth of the victim is 2004.
Further, the occurrence started to take place two years prior to that the date of examination of the victim.
That means on the date of occurrence, the victim was of 17 years.
The F.I.R. was lodged after long delay.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid materials, we are inclined to allow this interlocutory application.

Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellant, namely, Momin Ansari is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rs.
Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Palamau at Daltonganj in connection with Special POCSO Case No.19 of 2022 with a condition that the appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar,
Civil Court, Palamau at Daltonganj, once in every four months till the disposal of this appeal.
8. Accordingly, I.A. No. 9228 of 2024 stands allowed.
